title: Follow-up: we’re good at designing systems… but not running them
author: samnovakfit
selftext:
After going through all the replies, I feel like most tools mentioned are really good for designing stuff (Unity editor, Tiled, Miro, etc.), but not so much for actually running and managing systems long-term. Like, you can sketch levels, plan flows, place assets ,but once things grow, it gets messy fast. Iteration, consistency, tracking changes… that part still feels kinda manual.   
One comment about writing things down / structuring decisions actually made more sense than most tools tbh.   
It got me thinking more in a data-driven direction instead of just visual design.  
I’ve been checking out [Itembase.dev](http://Itembase.dev) recently , it’s not really a level design tool, but more about organizing game data (items, systems, etc.) in a structured way.  
Feels closer to solving the “how do we keep this system maintainable” problem rather than just “how do we design it”.  
Curious if anyone else is approaching it like this, or if you’re just sticking with traditional tools + docs?

comments.author: TheMcGarr
comments.body: I'm mocking my systems up in python before translating to a game engine
